The test contains a single Act operation (one call to CasamentoExato.forcaBruta) and a single assertion flow (fail if no exception, catch the expected exception). It focuses on a single behavior (expecting StringIndexOutOfBoundsException).

The test uses only local operations and no shared mutable state or test-order dependent naming. There are no @Before/@After annotations visible, and the method does not reference instance/static fields here, so it appears independent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class as shown contains only a single test method and exercises an exceptional flow. There is no corresponding happy-path test in the visible code to cover the normal flow for the same functionality.
The test uses a single set of inputs (a long literal string and 256) and does not exercise boundary values such as empty strings, zero, negative values, or extreme int values.

The test method is short and self-contained (< 10 lines) and there is no visible duplicated setup in multiple test methods in the provided snippet. While no helper methods are present, the single short test does not demonstrate duplication.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is small (well under 20 lines) and contains no loops or complex conditionals; it follows a single linear try-act-assert flow.

The test only checks for the occurrence of an exception (via fail/catch) and does not perform multiple assertions that verify different properties of the result or the exception (e.g., message contents or related state). This is superficial and may miss other faults.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations, no commented-out @Test methods shown, and the test is active (annotated with @Test). The header comment indicates maintenance effort.
The class-level Javadoc includes 'Traceability: REQ-ALG-001', which provides a requirement identifier linking tests to requirements.
